We launched the new Climate–Decent Work Risk Assessment visualisation last week, at the International Seminar on Human Trafficking: empirical evidence, measurement, and new theoretical debates.

What it does: climate hazard and working conditions on the same map of Brazil, at 5 km. Every cell carries a climate hazard score, a decent work score, and crop exposure for 117 crops from CROPGRIDS, combined following the IPCC's Risk = Hazard × Exposure × Vulnerability framing across all 5,570 municipalities. You zoom in and the hexagons get finer. You drag the lens and it tells you what is underneath it.

The project, the method and the data are all in the report: [https://zenodo.org/records/18839272](https://zenodo.org/records/18839272)

Every 5 km cell carries a climate hazard score (23 indicators in 9 groups — heat, UV, drought, flood, wildfire, air pollution, vector-borne disease, agrochemicals, WASH), a decent work score (35 indicators across the ILO's 10 decent work elements), and crop exposure for 117 crops from [CROPGRIDS](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41597-024-03247-7). The three combine following the IPCC's Risk = Hazard × Exposure × Vulnerability framework, covering all 5,570 municipalities. From the Clidewo project: Climate Change, Decent Work and Workers' Health in Brazilian Agriculture.
